note: Pilot/mid-work checkpoint. Filed after the live dry run and read-only diagnostics, before finalizing the mechanism resolution and close.

dryRunResult_authoritative.invocation: runParcelR5Zoning(process.env, { flags: parseParcelR5ZoningFlags(['--city','elgin-tx']) }) -- apply:false, the real exported job function, not a reimplementation.

thrown.message: Elgin/48021 residue is 36, above the declared 9 that was actually probed. The gap grew and the extra parcels have not been looked at -- re-probe and update the declaration rather than widening it.

dryRunResult_authoritative.verdict: Reproduces the dispatch's named refusal (execution dppvg) on Bastrop 48021. Confirmed real: the guard is not vacuous, and this specific number (36) is not a units mismatch -- see decomposition below.

diagnostic_zoneDecodeIntegrity.method: Reused the job's own exported HOIST_ZONES_SQL/HOIST_ZONES_COUNT_SQL against city_key='elgin-tx' to check for silent ST_MakeValid/ST_IsEmpty drops between raw staged rows and the decoded zone-polygon pool.
diagnostic_zoneDecodeIntegrity.result: raw staged rows (base layer, elgin-tx) = 3209, with geometry not null = 3209, decoded r5_zones_ok count = 3209. Zero drops. Rules out a decode-time defect as the explanation for the residue.

diagnostic_perCountyResidueByLayer.method: Reused CITY_ALL_PARCELS_SQL + CHUNK_ZONE_MATCH_SQL directly (same SQL constants the job exports), run to completion without invoking assertResidueWithinDeclaration, once per Elgin city_key row.
diagnostic_perCountyResidueByLayer.mechanismConfirmed: loadInScopeCities returns ONE ROW PER (place_fips, city_key), and Elgin has TWO staged base layers under two different city_keys (elgin-tx = FeatureServer/0 Bastrop-side, 3209 polygons; elgin-tx-travis = FeatureServer/1 Travis-side, 499 polygons, staged by CTX-STAGE2). Each row's population, via CITY_ALL_PARCELS_SQL, is scoped ONLY by place_fips -- the WHOLE city, both counties -- never intersected with the county the row's own layer actually covers. So every processCity call for Elgin spatial-joins THOUSANDS of parcels from the other county against a zone-polygon pool that cannot structurally cover them, manufacturing a large false residue for whichever county does not belong to that pass's layer. Bastrop's real residue against its OWN correct layer is 36; Travis's real residue against its OWN correct layer is 507 -- both close to instrument A/B's independent numbers (9/457 and 48-58/525 respectively). The 1680 and 3288 figures are pure cross-layer artifacts.
diagnostic_perCountyResidueByLayer.orderingHazard: assertResidueWithinDeclaration is called in a loop over layerGapByCounty (a Map whose insertion order follows CITY_ALL_PARCELS_SQL's ORDER BY county_fips ASC), so Bastrop (48021) is always checked before Travis (48453) within a single processCity call, and IN_SCOPE_CITIES_SQL's own ORDER BY (in_city_parcels DESC, no tiebreaker) does not deterministically order Elgin's two tied (5455-parcel) city_key rows relative to each other. A production sweep with no --city filter can therefore surface EITHER the real Bastrop number (36, if elgin-tx's row happens to process first) OR the wildly spurious cross-layer number (3288, if elgin-tx-travis processes first) for the SAME refusal code on the SAME underlying data, purely as a function of an unstable sort tie.

diagnostic_otherCitiesSameClass.method: SELECT city_geo_id, array_agg(DISTINCT city_key) FROM tx_zoning_district_staging WHERE layer_role='base' GROUP BY city_geo_id HAVING count(DISTINCT city_key) > 1.
diagnostic_otherCitiesSameClass.result: Exactly one city_geo_id (4823044 / Elgin) currently has more than one base-layer city_key. No other city in tx_zoning_district_staging is split across multiple layers today.
diagnostic_otherCitiesSameClass.caveat: This bounds CURRENT exposure, not the defect's scope. loadInScopeCities/processCity's failure to intersect a layer's county with its population is latent in the code for ANY future multi-county, multi-layer city, not specific to Elgin.
